newsitem.title: BELGIUM: The song remains the same for Belgian shares.
newsitem.headline: The song remains the same for Belgian shares.

text.p: Belgian shares shrugged off a wavering dollar to resume their upward treck on Monday on the back of stronger bonds and Wall Street's firmer close on Friday.
"There's nothing new under the sun," said Patricia Decolvenaer at De Maertelaere & Co.
At 0930 GMT the Bel-20 was up 0.38 percent, or 8.48 points, at 2,234.46 after earlier touching 2,238.24.
But volume was below par, totalling just 193 million francs.
"The market is dangerously empty. There's nothing on the selling side," Decolvenaer said.
The lack of volume on the ask side exacerbated the rise in holding company Gevaert, which was up 6.3 percent to 2,850 on a volume of merely 156 shares.

Dealers said the Belgian market's bullish behaviour continued to be fuelled by comments late last week by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan which assuaged fears over the near-term outlook for interest rates.
The dealers said the Bel-20 would continue to take its cue from Wall Street this week in the absence of any domestic factors to steer the market.
"Unless the U.S. start flipping, it looks like we'll continue to go straight higher," Decolvenaer said.
Oil firm Petrofina was unchanged at 12,775 francs ahead of its annual shareholders meeting later on Monday.
